options.text: A way to write plain JavaScript objects
A syntax extension that looks like HTML
A function to create React elements
A CSS preprocessor

questions.explanation: JSX is a syntax extension that lets you write HTML-like tags in JavaScript, which are compiled to React.createElement calls.

questions.prompt: Which statement about passing props is true?

options.text: Props can be mutated by the child component
Props are read-only in the receiving component
Props are only used in class components
Props can be passed as functions to trigger updates

questions.explanation: Props are immutable; the child component should not modify them, they are read-only.

questions.prompt: When calling setState, which of the following is correct?

options.text: setState immediately updates this.state
setState accepts an object or a function and updates state asynchronously
setState can be called outside a component method
setState returns the updated state value

questions.explanation: setState merges the given object or the result of a function into state and schedules an asynchronous update.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a valid way to define a React component?

options.text: function MyComponent(props) { return <div />; }
class MyComponent extends React.Component { render() { return <div />; } }
const MyComponent = (props) => { return <div />; }
var MyComponent = React.createClass({ render: function() { return <div />; } })

questions.explanation: React.createClass is deprecated and not used in modern React code.

options.text: It updates the DOM with new React elements without unmounting
It compiles JSX into JavaScript
It mounts a React component into a specified DOM container
It removes a component from the DOM

questions.explanation: ReactDOM.render mounts a React element into a DOM container and manages updates.

questions.prompt: Which lifecycle method is called after a component updates?

options.text: componentDidMount
componentWillUnmount
componentDidUpdate
componentWillReceiveProps

questions.explanation: componentDidUpdate runs after a component’s updates are flushed to the DOM.
